subject: Re: Request — vulnerability management evidence, scan cadence & CVE remediation SLA
messages:
From: Acme Security <security@acme.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: audit@sig.org
Date: 2026-10-20T15:12:00Z
Subject: Vulnerability management evidence request — Acme SOC2

Hi Markus,

As part of Acme's SOC 2 assessment we need evidence of Redwood's vulnerability management program focused on scanning cadence, ticketing and remediation SLAs. Specifically we need: 

- Scan cadence overview (authenticated vs unauthenticated, weekly vs monthly, scope for prod/non-prod).
- Export of recent scan results (CSV or PDF) covering last 90 days.
- The remediation tracker or ticketing evidence showing CVE triage + fix (Jira or tracker).
- A signed attestation confirming remediation SLAs for critical/high CVEs and the escalation path when SLAs are missed.

Deadline: can you provide the artifacts by end-of-day 2026-10-23 (Acme local time)? If you have per-CVE proof (Jira links, commit or patch IDs, deployment timestamps) that would be ideal.

Thanks,

Rachel Myers
Security Manager — Acme Corp
security@acme.com

--
Acme Security

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-20T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Vulnerability management evidence request — Acme SOC2

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver the artifacts by the requested date. High level: 

- Scan cadence: weekly authenticated scans against production exposure surface; full authenticated host scans monthly; unauthenticated external scans twice daily for public endpoints.
- Remediation SLAs: production-critical (CVSS 9.0+) — 72 hours; High (7.0–8.9) — 7 calendar days; Medium (4.0–6.9) — 30 days; Low — 90 days.

I’m looping in Laura (Security Ops) and Mina (Vuln Mgmt owner) to pull the export and remediation tracker. We will attach: Qualys CSV export (last 90 days), remediation-tracker.xlsx with per-CVE JIRA links, and a signed attestation PDF by end of day 2026-10-22 to give you time for review.

I’ll provide a short note on our CVE exception process and compensating controls as well. If you need a specific CSV format or additional filtering, tell us now.

— Markus Klein
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Mina / Karthik — heads up, Acme is requesting the usual artifacts for SOC2: recent scan exports, remediation tracker with per-CVE evidence, and a signed SLA attestation. Deadline is EOD 10/23.

Action items (please):
- Mina: pull Qualys/Scanner exports for the past 90 days (CSV preferred). Include: scan name, host/IP, CVE id, CVSS, scan date, status. File name: "2026-10-20-qualys-scan-summary.csv"
- Mina: export the remediation tracker with direct links to Jira tickets and include the resolution (commit hash or release tag) column. File name: "2026-10-21-remediation-tracker.xlsx"
- Karthik: confirm the per-environment scan schedules we published in the runbook (prod authenticated weekly, prod full monthly, non-prod weekly light scans) and add those notes into a short doc if needed.
- Markus: I will draft the attestation text; need your sign-off before we convert to PDF and sign.

Notes on SLAs we should attest to (internal guidance):
- Critical/Prod-critical (CVSS >= 9.0 or exploited in the wild): target remediation 72 hours after verification and assignment. Escalate immediately to on-call + Engineering Director if >24 hours to assign.
- High: target 7 calendar days.
- Medium: target 30 days.
- Low: target 90 days.

Proof-of-fix expectations: Jira ticket id + link, PR/commit hash or release tag, and deployment time (UTC). If exception applied, include approved exception ticket and compensating controls description.

Laura
Senior Security Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

Quick notes:
- Scan cadence: authenticated agent-based scans run weekly against the production host pool (snapshots taken Sunday 02:00 UTC), full authenticated host scans run on the first Saturday of each month, unauthenticated external endpoint scans run twice daily for public apps.
- Scanner details: Qualys v8.4 (authenticated), Nessus used for ad-hoc container image scans.
- Exceptions: we have an approved exceptions workflow (Jira project RED-EXC). Exceptions include compensating controls and expiry dates; the remediation-tracker.xlsx includes a column for exception ticket ids where applicable.

I also exported a short per-CVE evidence column with the following format: Jira Link | PR/Commit | Deployed Tag | Deployed At (UTC). We included this for CVEs marked High and Critical in the 90-day window.

If Acme needs a different CSV schema, say additional columns or normalized hostnames, tell me and I’ll regenerate.

Rachel — attaching the artifact packet we discussed and our signed attestation. Summary below and attachments included.

Summary (what's attached):
- 2026-10-20-qualys-scan-summary.csv — authenticated/unauthenticated scan exports (last 90 days).
- 2026-10-21-remediation-tracker.xlsx — per-CVE tracker with Jira links and proof-of-fix columns (PR/commit, release tag, deployed timestamp).
- 2026-10-22-vm-attestation-signed.pdf — signed attestation confirming SLAs and escalation process.

Attested SLAs (as signed):
- Production critical (CVSS >= 9.0 or known active exploitation): 72 hours to remediation.
- High: 7 calendar days.
- Medium: 30 calendar days.
- Low: 90 calendar days.

Escalation: If an assigned critical/high CVE is unremediated past SLA, the ticket automatically escalates to Engineering Director and Product Security on-call; emergency patch plan and rollback playbooks are initiated for production-impacting fixes.

Per-CVE evidence: the tracker includes Jira links (RED-xxxx), a PR/Commit column and deployed tag + UTC timestamp. Example links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-2345 (attached in tracker).

Let me know if Acme wants a short walkthrough call — we can do a 20-minute session to walk the artifacts next week.

Regards,

— Markus Klein
